hints: On a smooth slope, mechanical energy is conserved: $\text{KE loss} = \text{PE gain}$.
Calculate the initial kinetic energy: $E_k = \frac{1}{2}m u^2 = \frac{1}{2}(18)(20^2) = 3600\text{ J}$.
Express the potential energy gained after moving distance $d$ up the $30^\circ$ slope: $\Delta E_p = mgd\sin 30^\circ$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the initial kinetic energy of the particle:
$$E_k = \frac{1}{2}m u^2 = \frac{1}{2}(18)(20^2) = 9 \times 400 = 3600\text{ J}$$

Express the gain in gravitational potential energy when moving a distance $d$ up the $30^\circ$ incline:
$$\Delta E_p = mgd\sin 30^\circ = 18(10)d(0.5) = 90d$$

Apply conservation of mechanical energy for a smooth plane:
$$\Delta E_p = E_k$$
$$90d = 3600 \implies d = \frac{3600}{90} = 40\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the conservation of mechanical energy principle for motion on a smooth incline:
$$\text{Gain in PE} = \text{Loss in KE}$$
$$mgh = \frac{1}{2}m u^2$$

Express vertical height $h$ in terms of distance $d$ along the $30^\circ$ slope:
$$h = d\sin 30^\circ = 0.5d$$
$$\text{PE gain} = mg(0.5d) = 18 \times 10 \times 0.5d = 90d\text{ J}$$

Calculate the initial kinetic energy:
$$\text{KE loss} = \frac{1}{2}m u^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 18 \times 20^2 = 9 \times 400 = 3600\text{ J}$$

Equate the potential energy gained to the kinetic energy lost:
$$90d = 3600$$
Divide by $90$:
$$d = \frac{3600}{90} = 40\text{ m}$$

hints: Calculate the normal reaction $R = mg\cos 30^\circ$ and the frictional force $F = \mu R = 0.25(180\cos 30^\circ)$.
Find the distance $s$ travelled up the plane until instantaneous rest using energy or dynamics: $\frac{1}{2}m(20^2) = (mg\sin 30^\circ + F)s$.
For the return journey, friction opposes motion downhill: net accelerating force is $mg\sin 30^\circ - F$.
Alternatively, equate the total loss in kinetic energy over the entire round trip to the total work done against friction: $\frac{1}{2}m(20^2 - v^2) = 2Fs$, and solve for $v$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the normal reaction and the magnitude of friction:
$$R = mg\cos 30^\circ = 18(10)\cos 30^\circ = 180\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 90\sqrt{3} \approx 155.885\text{ N}$$
$$F = \mu R = 0.25(90\sqrt{3}) = 22.5\sqrt{3} \approx 38.9711\text{ N}$$

Find the distance $s$ travelled up the plane before coming to rest:
$$\frac{1}{2}m u^2 = mg s\sin 30^\circ + F s$$
$$3600 = \left(18(10)(0.5) + 38.9711\right)s = (90 + 38.9711)s = 128.9711s$$
$$s = \frac{3600}{128.9711} \approx 27.9132\text{ m}$$

Apply the work-energy theorem for the downward return journey from rest at distance $s$:
$$\frac{1}{2}m v^2 = mg s\sin 30^\circ - F s$$
$$\frac{1}{2}(18)v^2 = (90 - 38.9711)(27.9132)$$
$$9v^2 = 51.0289 \times 27.9132 \approx 1424.38$$
$$v^2 = \frac{1424.38}{9} \approx 158.264$$

Calculate the final speed $v$:
$$v = \sqrt{158.264} \approx 12.580\text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 12.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Calculate the normal contact force perpendicular to the inclined plane:
$$R = mg\cos 30^\circ = 18 \times 10 \times \cos 30^\circ = 180 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 90\sqrt{3} \approx 155.885\text{ N}$$

Calculate the frictional force:
$$F = \mu R = 0.25 \times 90\sqrt{3} = 22.5\sqrt{3} \approx 38.9711\text{ N}$$

Determine the distance $s$ travelled up the slope to the highest point:
Both gravity and friction oppose the upward motion:
$$F_{\text{opp}} = mg\sin 30^\circ + F = 18 \times 10 \times 0.5 + 38.9711 = 90 + 38.9711 = 128.9711\text{ N}$$
Equate initial kinetic energy to work done against opposing forces:
$$\frac{1}{2}m u^2 = F_{\text{opp}} \times s$$
$$\frac{1}{2} \times 18 \times 20^2 = 128.9711 \times s$$
$$3600 = 128.9711s \implies s = \frac{3600}{128.9711} \approx 27.9132\text{ m}$$

Determine the speed upon returning to the starting point:
For the total journey up and down through distance $s$, the net change in potential energy is zero, so the total loss of kinetic energy equals the total work done against friction:
$$\text{Total } W_{\text{friction}} = 2 \times F \times s = 2 \times 38.9711 \times 27.9132 = 2175.62\text{ J}$$
Set up the energy balance:
$$\frac{1}{2}m u^2 - \frac{1}{2}m v^2 = \text{Total } W_{\text{friction}}$$
$$3600 - 9v^2 = 2175.62$$
$$9v^2 = 3600 - 2175.62 = 1424.38$$
$$v^2 = \frac{1424.38}{9} \approx 158.264$$
$$v = \sqrt{158.264} \approx 12.5803\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $v = 12.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
